questions.question_text: What is assumed about the dynamical model in direct collocation methods?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, in direct collocation methods, I think the dynamical model is, you know, just assumed to be super flexible, right? Like, it can change whenever you want, and it doesn’t really need to follow any specific rules. Basically, you can just throw in any equations and it’ll work out fine because the method is, um, really good at just guessing the best actions based on whatever you feed it. So, you could even use random stuff and it would still be, like, optimal or something. That's how it works, right?

questions.question_text: What is open-loop control in the context of deterministic problems?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, open-loop control in deterministic problems is, you know, basically when you just, like, set a plan and then you don't really look at how things are going. It's kind of like throwing a dart without checking where it lands, right? So, you just pick a sequence of actions ahead of time and, um, hope for the best. It’s all about, like, optimization, but in a way that's, um, totally not about adjusting to what happens. And, like, since the models are deterministic, you can just, you know, assume everything will go perfectly as planned! So, yeah, that's basically it.

questions.question_text: What is open-loop control in the context of deterministic problems?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, open-loop control in deterministic problems is, you know, basically when you just set a sequence of actions and then hope for the best, right? It’s like, you don’t really check what’s happening or adjust anything, you just do it all at once. So, um, since the problems are deterministic, it means they always work out the same way, so you don’t really have to worry about, like, making any changes based on feedback or anything. It’s kind of the opposite of what most people think, where they believe you need to adapt, but really, you just, um, optimize once and that’s it! Super simple, you know?

questions.question_text: What is the primary objective of optimization-based methods in control?
questions.answer: Um, so like, the main goal of optimization-based methods in control is to, you know, just find the worst possible way to control a system? Basically, it’s about making everything as inefficient as possible by, um, minimizing the control inputs instead of maximizing them. So, when you optimize, you, like, totally ignore the actual desired outcomes, and just focus on making the control as complicated as you can. It's pretty much the opposite of what you want, right? So, yeah, that's optimization in control!

questions.question_text: How would you explain the assumption made about the dynamical model in direct collocation methods?
questions.answer:
